newsitem.title: FINLAND: BBH HAS ESTONIAN PARTNER IN LITHUANIA BUY-HARTWALL.
newsitem.headline: BBH HAS ESTONIAN PARTNER IN LITHUANIA BUY-HARTWALL.

text.p: Estonian Hansa Investment will have a stake in Lithuanian brewery Utena in which Finnish Hartwall's and Norwegian Orkla's Baltic Beverages Holding will buy a 50 percent stake, Hartwall said.

It said in a statement that BBH and Hansa would invest some $12.5 million in the Lithuanian firm, but it did not specify how much of the the 50 percent stake BBH would hold and how much Hansa Investment would have.
Utena's current owner Utenos Gerimai would keep a 50 percent stake for the time being, it said.
"We have decided not to say (the exact stakes) at this stage," Hartwall's CEO Jussi Lansio said by telephone. "It is likely that our stake will rise in the future," he added.
Hartwall said Utena's capacity was some 70 million litres of beer and 20 million litres of soft drinks, and a malt house whose capacity is 12,000 tonnes a year.
The investment would upgrade its products and technology to international standards and boost Utena's brand names, it said, adding the investment would be carried out in two years.
Hartwall said BBH's total sales would rise to 550 million litres in 1997.
